text:
maria.dev: Quick one — I switched our client to use Basic auth (trying to reuse some internal tooling) and streaming responses keep failing with 401 after ~1-2s. Works fine with Bearer. Anyone seen a Basic auth quirk that would cause mid-stream auth failures?

alex.engineering: Did you construct the header with `-u`/`--user` in curl or manually set `Authorization:`? `curl -u $API_KEY:` will base64 encode a trailing colon (api_key:) which is allowed, but some servers expect Bearer only.

maria.dev: I'd been doing `curl -u $API_KEY:` on macOS and `fetch` in Node with `Authorization: 'Basic ' + Buffer.from(process.env.API_KEY + ':').toString('base64')`. Same approach in both, but Node stream crashes with 401 mid-stream (server returns data then 401 chunk).

sam.sdk: Two quick possibilities: (1) trailing newline/BOM in the env var meaning the header doesn't match expected value; (2) the service doing an auth re-check on a follow-up request and the header differs on streaming reconnects (e.g., if a proxy strips headers on chunked replay).

jenna.devex: Also check if your client automatically retries with a different request header set on reconnection. Some streaming libs detach custom headers on subsequent range/continuation requests.

alex.engineering: Can you paste the curl + node examples? small commands are easiest to spot quoting issues.

maria.dev: sure — here's the exact commands I ran: 
```bash
# curl on mac
curl -N -u "$API_KEY:" 
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" 
  https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/stream
```
and node: 
```js
const res = await fetch(url, {
  headers: {
    Authorization: 'Basic ' + Buffer.from(process.env.API_KEY + ':').toString('base64'),
    Accept: 'text/event-stream'
  }
});
// then pipe res.body to process.stdout
```

sam.sdk: One obvious check: log `JSON.stringify(process.env.API_KEY)` to ensure there are no invisible chars. On mac `echo $API_KEY | od -c` will show \r\n or BOM. If you created the secret via a GUI or copied from a file with CRLF you'll get `\r` at the end which makes the base64 mismatch.

maria.dev: confirmed `od -c` shows `n e w k e y \n`. I thought `Buffer.from(...).toString('base64')` would ignore newline? But base64 input includes the newline so header changes.

alex.engineering: Right — `echo` adds newline. Use `printf '%s' "$API_KEY"` or `echo -n` (but `echo -n` is shell-specific). In JS you can `process.env.API_KEY.trim()` or better, ensure the secret has no trailing newline when stored.

sam.sdk: Also watch out for Windows/WSL vs mac behavior: `pbpaste` / `pbcopy` sometimes includes an extra newline depending on how you copied it. And GitHub Actions secrets sometimes get newlines if you added them with a trailing newline in the UI.

maria.dev: OK trimming fixed the immediate 401 problem for the initial connection, but I'm still occasionally seeing a 401 about 30s later during long streams. Any ideas?

jenna.devex: Do you have any proxy or CDN in front? Some proxies buffer and then re-issue requests, and certain proxy configs drop or rewrite `Authorization` on subsequent internal requests. A quick check is to hit the instance directly (bypass CDN) and see if it reproduces.

alex.engineering: Another angle: Basic auth uses username:password base64. If you supply an empty password (api_key:) that's valid. But some server stacks validate that the credential username is an actual user and may trigger session checks later. Redwood recommends Bearer tokens for API keys — prefer `Authorization: Bearer <KEY>` to avoid backend framework Basic auth hooks.

maria.dev: ah that makes sense. We switched because our infra has a helper that sets Basic quickly with `curl -u`. I'll try Bearer everywhere.

sam.sdk: If you must use Basic for tooling, ensure the header is stable across reconnects. Example robust header generation (POSIX):
```bash
# create header without newline, safe across shells
H=$(printf '%s:' "$API_KEY" | base64 -w0)
curl -N -H "Authorization: Basic $H" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" https://...
```
On mac `base64 -w0` is `-b 0` for GNU vs BSD differences; on macOS use `base64` (no wrap) or `base64 | tr -d '\n'` to be safe.

maria.dev: thanks — small followups: (1) Is `-u` adding any extra behavior besides building header? (2) Why would server accept first chunks then later reject?

alex.engineering: (1) `-u username:password` sets `Authorization` header only for the first request; if curl follows redirects it may drop or re-add the header depending on `--location` behavior. Also some HTTP clients do an initial request without credentials to see if 401 is returned, then resend with credentials — differences can matter with streaming endpoints.

(2) If there's a keep-alive health check or a reconnection initiated by a load balancer, the follow-up request might be routed to another backend that has stricter auth checks or is misconfigured. Or a token mismatch if you rotated keys mid-stream.

jenna.devex: CI note — if you're testing in GH Actions, secrets interpolation can add quotes. Example bad: `-H "Authorization: Basic '$H'"` in a workflow step will send literal single quotes. Use `${{ secrets.API_KEY }}` without extra quotes and check `run: echo "${{ secrets.API_KEY }}" | od -c` in a debug step (don't print real secret in prod logs).

ci-bot: Reminder: avoid printing full secrets in public logs. Use masking or echo length/checksum only.

maria.dev: Great, switching to Bearer + trimmed env var fixed both the immediate and later 401s when testing against the origin. I'll leave a short note in the repo README about preferring Bearer and `printf`/`trim()` tips. Thanks all :thumbsup:

sam.sdk: One-liner to add to README: `# prefer Bearer tokens for SDKs; if using Basic ensure no trailing newline: Authorization: Basic $(printf '%s:' "$API_KEY" | base64 | tr -d '\n')`

alex.engineering: Also add a tiny test that opens a 60s stream in CI to catch regressions.

maria.dev: Will do — closing this thread.
